leads.summary: Lock hooks miss the suspend and shell-recovery lock entrypoints
leads.consequence: A suspend initiated without a preceding lid/idle/manual lock runs bin/omarchy-system-sleep-monitor:7-15 -> omarchy-system-sleep-lock:63-83,109-124 -> omarchy-shell lock lock directly, never omarchy-system-lock. Shell recovery uses bin/omarchy-restart-shell:45-61 similarly. An enabled credential-clearing lock hook does not run on these successful locks. The lid path alone can incidentally invoke it first. Consider dispatching from the lock service at secure transition or explicitly covering the alternate paths, with deduplication.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F1 (suspend/hibernate); shell-restart relock part checked by coordinator and not published separately (it re-secures an already locked session)

leads.summary: Existing accounts never receive the new lock sample on upgrade
leads.consequence: Settings PKGBUILD copies config/** into /etc/skel and /usr/share/omarchy/config, not into an existing account. The package update provides no lock.d migration. Such users cannot follow the sample's instruction to remove .sample in ~/.config because it is absent, while a new user has it; only an explicit destructive config reset or manual copy obtains it. Add a non-clobbering migration/copy or document the exact per-file install command for upgraded users.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus N4; precedent, not a defect; dropped

leads.summary: The end-user hook event list omits lock
leads.consequence: The published manual lists all six prior named hook events and explains how to enable their .sample files, but does not list lock, while only the agent skill gets a new entry. Users relying on the manual will not discover the new hook or its background timing. Add a lock row and describe the sample's availability on upgraded accounts.

leads.summary: Combined with open #9429, the hook still fires before security verification
leads.consequence: #9429 requests a lock, does cleanup, then checks missing-pam and polls the secure state before reporting success/failure. The two production changes merge without conflict but place this PR's credential-clearing hook immediately after the initial request and before #9429's missing-pam check and secure poll. Thus missing-pam or a timed-out, never-secure session still runs the 'after lock' hook. The combined tests have two conflicts and must be resolved together; place the hook on the secure-success path after the state check, and add an assertion it is absent on failure.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus #9429 note; published in Details

leads.summary: Combined with #9575, the system-lock test requires a manual merge to keep both checks
leads.consequence: #9575 adds --skip-shell-request to the same production command and a second test case after the existing last assertion. Production merges cleanly with the hook still firing in both command modes, but git merge-file reports a conflict exactly between its appended test and this PR's appended hook test. If resolving by taking either side, coverage of either the hook or the skip path is lost. Keep both test cases and assert hook dispatch for the skip-shell-request path.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus #9575 note; published in Details

leads.summary: The new hooks.md sibling entry conflicts with #6662's insertion
leads.consequence: Open #6662 inserts hyprland-config.d immediately after font-set.d on the same unchanged context where this PR inserts lock.d. A three-way merge of the files produced a conflict at lines 16-20. Resolve by keeping both lines in the event list; neither hook needs to be dropped. leads.triage: new; verified by coordinator (sol/merge6662-hooks.md, head hooks.md:14-16) and by Opus during the self-check (git merge-tree); published in Details

leads.summary: New system-lock test cannot detect a synchronous, blocking hook
leads.consequence: Replace the backgrounded call at bin/omarchy-system-lock:12 with an otherwise identical foreground call. The omarchy-hook stub merely appends one line and exits, so the 20-poll loop, hook-presence check and first-line check still succeed even though arbitrary slow user hooks now block the lock helper and its following keyboard/screensaver cleanup. Add a blocking hook stub and assert the lock command proceeds with cleanup before unblocking it, without leaking a child into later cases.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F2; published as optional test improvement

leads.summary: The timing assertion only checks first logged request, not a secure screen
leads.consequence: The test's omarchy-shell stub logs the request and exits without ever reporting lock security. The actual shell's lock() may answer missing-pam/failed or ok while beginLock merely queues the Wayland session lock; secure is signaled later. This test passes even when the hook fires while the session remains unlocked, so its pass message 'after locking' and the sample's line 3 make a stronger promise than the code checks. Poll lock status or observe the service secure event before firing the hook, then test that ordering with a stub exposing the transition.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus N1; published as optional note

leads.summary: Enabled sample reload clears SSH and smart-card PIN cache, not only OpenPGP passphrases
leads.consequence: On an account using gpg-agent for SSH or card PIN caching, RELOADAGENT calls agent_flush_cache(0), which clears every cache entry including SSH and PIN modes, then reloads configuration and can stop scdaemon when disabled. Users opting into a GPG passphrase hook also lose those cached credentials and may face extra SSH/card prompts after each screen lock. If broad eviction is intended, explicitly warn in the sample; otherwise use narrower per-cache-ID clearing (which requires known IDs). The sample remains disabled unless renamed.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus G2/N2; published as optional note

# RETRO: PR #13513 (team 5)

## What worked

- Opus and the Sol hunter ran in parallel. Sol finished in 9 minutes, and 8 of its 9 leads corroborated Opus. The one new lead (#6662 `hooks.md` conflict) was cheap to verify.
- The Opus self-check caught five real wording errors, including a lost qualifier in the main finding's impact and an overclaim in an optional note that came from Opus's own first handback.

## Avoidable friction and incidents

- **Host command execution by the coordinator (serious).** An unquoted heredoc (`python3 - <<EOF`) around draft text with Markdown backticks made bash run `omarchy-system-lock`, `omarchy-system-sleep-lock`, `omarchy-shell lock lock` and `omarchy-hook lock` on the live host. Fix: coordinators must always quote heredoc delimiters (`<<'EOF'`), or write edit scripts to a file first and pass paths as arguments. Suggested addition to the workflow's coordinator rules.
- `review_team.visible_length` does not handle nested `<details>` blocks (it counted 1,911 against a nesting-aware 1,492). Either document "no nested details" in comment-requirements.md or make the measure nesting-aware. Tool bug candidate.
- The first editorial check correctly moved the test-only finding into a collapsed Optional test improvement. Drafting could apply this up front: test-only gaps are optional notes, not visible findings.

## Carry forward

- Quote every heredoc delimiter.
- Keep test-only gaps collapsed from the first draft.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** Suspend and hibernate lock the session without running `lock.d` hooks.

### Suspend and hibernate skip the lock hook

Suspend and hibernate (including the System menu entries) lock via `omarchy-system-sleep-lock`, which calls `omarchy-shell lock lock` directly and never runs `omarchy-hook`. **Impact:** with the gpg sample enabled, cached passphrases survive a menu suspend. An undocked lid close is not affected.

**Suggested change:** run `omarchy-hook lock` detached from `beginLock()` in `shell/plugins/lock/Service.qml`, which every new lock goes through (like #13156's layout reset).

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at a8a01d49)</summary>

Reproducer: the suspend/hibernate lock path does not run `lock.d` hooks (reviewed head a8a01d49).

Save as `test/shell.d/sleep-lock-hook-test.sh` in a checkout of the PR head and run `bash test/shell.d/sleep-lock-hook-test.sh` (needs `rg`, like `system-lock-test.sh`, and `jq`, which `omarchy-system-sleep-lock` uses to read the lock status). It drives `bin/omarchy-system-sleep-lock`, which `omarchy-sleep-lock.service` runs on PrepareForSleep, with a stub shell that reports the session secure, and checks whether `omarchy-hook lock` was called.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmpdir"' EXIT

mock_bin="$tmpdir/bin"
call_log="$tmpdir/calls"
mkdir -p "$mock_bin"

for command in omarchy-hook omarchy-hyprland-monitor-clamshell omarchy-notification-send; do
  cat >"$mock_bin/$command" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
printf '%s %s\n' "$(basename "$0")" "$*" >>"$CALL_LOG"
SH
done

cat >"$mock_bin/omarchy-shell" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
printf '%s %s\n' "$(basename "$0")" "$*" >>"$CALL_LOG"
[[ $* == "lock status" ]] && printf '{"secure":true,"requested":true}\n'
exit 0
SH
chmod +x "$mock_bin"/*

# Suspend and hibernate (System menu, systemctl suspend) lock the session here,
# from omarchy-sleep-lock.service, without going through omarchy-system-lock.
PATH="$mock_bin:$PATH" CALL_LOG="$call_log" "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-system-sleep-lock" 2000 ||
  fail "sleep lock secures the session" "calls: $(tr '\n' ';' <"$call_log")"
sleep 0.5

rg -q '^omarchy-hook lock' "$call_log" ||
  fail "locking before suspend runs the lock hook" "calls: $(tr '\n' ';' <"$call_log")"
pass "locking before suspend runs the lock hook"
```

Actual output at a8a01d49 (exit status 1):

```
calls: omarchy-shell lock lock;omarchy-hyprland-monitor-clamshell ;omarchy-shell lock status;
not ok - locking before suspend runs the lock hook
```

The session is locked (`lock lock`, then `lock status` reports secure and the script exits 0), but `omarchy-hook` is never called. This test only demonstrates the gap. If the hook call moves into the shell's lock service, a test of that location would replace it.

</details>

### The manual does not list the `lock` event

`lock` is added only to the agent skill's `hooks.md`, not to the hook table in `manual/31-dotfiles.md`. **Impact:** manual readers will not find the event.

**Suggested change:** add a `lock` row to that table.

<details><summary>Optional test improvement: the new test misses a foreground hook</summary>

**Optional test improvement:** `system-lock-test.sh` still passes with the trailing `&` removed from the hook line, because the stub hook returns at once, so a slow hook blocking the lock would go unnoticed. A stub hook that sleeps, plus an assertion that `omarchy-system-lock` returns quickly, catches it:


Reproducer: the new test in `test/shell.d/system-lock-test.sh` still passes when the lock hook is no longer run in the background (reviewed head a8a01d49).

Step 1. In a checkout of the PR head, drop the trailing `&` from the hook line, so a slow hook blocks the rest of the lock:

```bash
sed -i 's|^omarchy-hook lock >/dev/null 2>&1 &$|omarchy-hook lock >/dev/null 2>\&1|' bin/omarchy-system-lock
bash test/shell.d/system-lock-test.sh
```

Actual output with that change (exit status 0):

```
ok - system lock waits for ttfx before closing its terminal
ok - system lock runs the lock hook after locking
```

Step 2. A test whose stub hook takes a while catches it. Save as `test/shell.d/system-lock-hook-background-test.sh`:

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmpdir"' EXIT

mock_bin="$tmpdir/bin"
call_log="$tmpdir/calls"
mkdir -p "$mock_bin"

for command in omarchy-shell hyprctl pkill timeout; do
  cat >"$mock_bin/$command" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
printf '%s %s\n' "$(basename "$0")" "$*" >>"$CALL_LOG"
SH
done

# A hook that takes a while. Closing its output lets the script's own
# redirection decide whether anything is still waiting on it.
cat >"$mock_bin/omarchy-hook" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
printf '%s %s\n' "$(basename "$0")" "$*" >>"$CALL_LOG"
exec >/dev/null 2>&1
sleep 5
SH

cat >"$mock_bin/pgrep" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
exit 1
SH
chmod +x "$mock_bin"/*

start=$SECONDS
PATH="$mock_bin:$PATH" CALL_LOG="$call_log" "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-system-lock"
(( SECONDS - start < 3 )) ||
  fail "a slow lock hook does not hold up the lock" "took $((SECONDS - start))s"
pass "a slow lock hook does not hold up the lock"

for _ in {1..20}; do
  rg -q '^omarchy-hook ' "$call_log" && break
  sleep 0.1
done
mapfile -t calls <"$call_log"
[[ ${calls[0]} == "omarchy-shell lock lock" && " ${calls[*]} " == *" omarchy-hook lock "* ]] ||
  fail "system lock runs the lock hook after locking" "calls: ${calls[*]}"
pass "system lock runs the lock hook after locking"
```

Actual output at the unmodified head a8a01d49 (exit status 0):

```
ok - a slow lock hook does not hold up the lock
ok - system lock runs the lock hook after locking
```

Actual output with the Step 1 change (exit status 1):

```
took 5s
not ok - a slow lock hook does not hold up the lock
```

Related: with the hook line moved above `omarchy-shell lock lock` but still backgrounded, the PR's ordering check passed 13 of 30 runs, because the background hook and the lock request race to write the call log first.

</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified** (sandbox runs with stubbed desktop commands):
- The hook starts after `omarchy-shell lock lock` returns and runs in the background: with a 2-second hook, `omarchy-system-lock` exited in about 12 ms and the hook finished after it.
- `omarchy-hook` skips the shipped `.sample`, and runs it once renamed.
- Against a private gpg-agent 2.4.9, the renamed sample emptied the passphrase cache: a cache-only sign failed afterwards, and the agent kept its PID.
- The PR's test passed 30 of 30 runs, and fails when the hook call is removed, misnamed, or moved in front of the lock in the foreground.

**Optional notes:**
- The hook starts when the lock is requested, not once it is secure. It also runs when the shell refuses the lock (for example `missing-pam`) and on every call while already locked. Running it from `beginLock()` fixes the last two; starting it when the lock turns secure (`onSecureStateChanged`) would fix all three. Otherwise, `hooks.md` could say "when a lock is requested; may run more than once".
- `RELOADAGENT` flushes every gpg-agent cache entry, including SSH key passphrases, but does not reset scdaemon, so an OpenPGP card PIN verified before locking is not asked for again for decryption or SSH authentication (from GnuPG source; not tested on hardware). `gpgconf --reload scdaemon` would cover card users.

**Related open PRs** (three-way merges with this head):
- #9575 and #9429: textual conflicts in `test/shell.d/system-lock-test.sh`. With #9429, `bin/omarchy-system-lock` merges automatically with the hook before #9429's wait for a secure lock, so the hook would also run when that wait fails. The merged test must still stub `omarchy-hook`.
- #6662: both PRs add a line after `font-set.d/` in `hooks.md`. Keep both lines.

</details>
